problems: concepts[Pronoun case].tip: The 'drop the other person' test does not work with 'between', because 'between' always needs two objects ('between me' alone is not a sentence you can test). The tip applies the wrong method to the example and can confuse learners.
summary[1]: "Subject-verb agreement and pronoun agreement are the biggest areas" is an unverifiable claim. ETS does not publish how many questions each grammar rule gets.
Minor (not a fail): pronoun agreement is described as number only; standard rule also covers person and gender. Not incorrect as written.
Minor (not a fail): adjective/adverb tip does not mention linking verbs (feel bad, look good), but 'usually' hedges it.
summary[2] last sentence: "Among correct choices, pick the shortest one that keeps the meaning" is too absolute. It conflicts with concepts[Concise wording], which says 'usually'.
concepts[Semicolon and colon].tip: "Full sentence on both sides" is too absolute, because semicolons also separate list items that already contain commas.
Minor (not a fail): 'A modifier must sit next to the word it describes' is an absolute simplification of the usual rule; acceptable as plain-English guidance.
Minor (not a fail): semicolon definition omits its use between list items that contain commas; not incorrect as written.
